unit_description: This unit applies addition and subtraction to real-world problem solving. Students decide which operation to use, estimate before solving, and handle one-step and two-step problems with unknown numbers.
unit_goals: Decide whether a problem requires addition or subtraction.
Estimate before solving to check reasonableness.
Solve one-step addition and subtraction word problems.
Solve two-step problems with unknown numbers.

weeks.weekly_focus: Students use addition and subtraction to solve word problems, estimate first, and handle two-step and unknown-number problems.

lessons.lesson_title: Decide Whether to Add or Subtract
lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by identifying the operation in short story problems.
lessons.concept: Word problems give clues about the operation. Words like 'total,' 'altogether,' or 'how many more' help you decide whether to add or subtract.
lessons.practice: Read word problems and choose the correct operation before solving.
lessons.objective: Decide whether to add or subtract in a word problem.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by choosing the operation.

questions.prompt: Mia has 24 stickers. She buys 15 more. Should you add or subtract?
A box has 90 books. 37 are given away. Should you add or subtract?
What is the difference between 58 and 32?

learn.title: Decide Whether to Add or Subtract
teaching_points: Ask: am I combining or taking apart?
Match the story to the operation.

example.prompt: Sara has 45 pages read. She reads 28 more. How many pages has she read?

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: A jar has 120 marbles. 45 marbles fall out. How many are left?

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: For each problem, choose the operation and solve.

flashcards.title: Operation Clues
flashcards.instructions: Review words that tell you to add or subtract.

bigIdea.title: Decide Whether to Add or Subtract
bigIdea.subtitle: Use clue words to choose
bigIdea.intro: Every word problem has hidden clues. Words like total and more point to addition. Words like left, difference, and fewer point to subtraction.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How do clue words help you solve word problems?

ruleCards.description: These words mean you are putting groups together.

ruleCards.equation: left, fewer, difference, how many more
ruleCards.description: These words mean you are comparing or taking away.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by rounding numbers to the nearest ten and hundred.
lessons.concept: Estimating before solving helps you know if your answer is reasonable. Round the numbers, do the easier calculation, and compare.
lessons.practice: Estimate the answer to word problems before finding the exact answer.
lessons.objective: Estimate to check reasonableness before solving.

questions.prompt: Estimate 187 + 214 by rounding to the nearest hundred.
Estimate 403 - 198 by rounding to the nearest hundred.

learn.title: Estimate Before Solving
teaching_points: Round the numbers in the problem.
Use the estimate to check your exact answer.

example.prompt: A school has 236 boys and 287 girls. About how many students?

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: A bakery had 420 cupcakes. It sold 189. About how many are left?

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Estimate first, then solve each word problem.

bigIdea.title: Estimate Before Solving
bigIdea.subtitle: Round first to check your answer
bigIdea.intro: A quick estimate is like a friendly check. If your exact answer is far from the estimate, you know to look again.

ruleCards.description: Round each number to a nearby ten or hundred.
Compare the exact answer to the estimate to see if it makes sense.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by solving one-step addition and subtraction equations.
lessons.concept: A one-step problem can be solved with a single equation. Identify the numbers, choose the operation, and solve.
lessons.practice: Solve a variety of one-step addition and subtraction word problems.
lessons.objective: Solve one-step addition and subtraction word problems.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by solving one-step problems.

questions.prompt: Tom has 38 baseball cards. He gives away 12. How many does he have left?
A bus has 45 seats. 18 are empty. How many are filled?
There are 56 apples in one basket and 37 in another. How many apples are there in all?

learn.title: One-Step Addition and Subtraction Problems
teaching_points: Read the problem for the important numbers.
Choose the operation based on the action.
Write an equation and solve it.

example.prompt: A farmer has 125 apples. She sells 48 apples. How many are left?

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: A bookshelf has 92 books. 35 are chapter books. The rest are picture books. How many are picture books?

flashcards.title: One-Step Problem Words
flashcards.instructions: Review key words for one-step problems.

bigIdea.title: One-Step Addition and Subtraction Problems
bigIdea.subtitle: One action, one equation
bigIdea.intro: One-step problems have one action. Find the numbers, choose the operation, and write one equation to solve.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How is a one-step problem different from a two-step problem?

ruleCards.description: Find the numbers you know and the question you need to answer.
Use one equation to solve a one-step problem.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by solving two short equations in a row.
lessons.concept: Two-step problems need two actions. Sometimes the unknown is in the middle. Solve the first step, then use that answer for the second step.
lessons.practice: Solve two-step addition and subtraction problems with unknowns.
lessons.objective: Solve two-step word problems with unknown numbers.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by working through two steps.

questions.prompt: A store had 80 shirts. It sold 25 in the morning and 18 in the afternoon. How many are left?
Leo had $50. He spent $18 and then earned $12. How much does he have now?
There are 72 children on a bus. 15 get off and 9 get on. How many are on the bus now?

learn.title: Two-Step Problems with Unknown Numbers
teaching_points: Use the result for the next action.
Keep track of the unknown at each step.

example.prompt: A class has 28 students. 5 leave and 7 arrive. How many are in the class now?

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: A fish tank has 45 fish. 12 are removed and 8 new ones are added. How many fish are there now?

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Solve each two-step problem. Show both steps.

bigIdea.title: Two-Step Problems with Unknown Numbers
bigIdea.subtitle: Solve one step, then the next
bigIdea.intro: Some problems have two actions. Solve the first part, then use that answer in the second part. Watch for unknown amounts in the middle.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How do you keep track of an unknown in a two-step problem?

ruleCards.description: Find the result of the first action before moving on.
Use the answer from the first step to complete the second step.

lessons.lesson_title: Unit Evaluation: Addition and Subtraction Applications
lessons.fact_drill: Rapid review of choosing operations, estimating, one-step, and two-step problem solving.
lessons.concept: Review the four problem-solving skills from this unit: choosing operations, estimating, one-step, and two-step problems with unknowns.
lessons.practice: Complete a balanced evaluation covering the skills from this unit.
lessons.objective: Show what you know about addition and subtraction problem solving.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Get ready to show what you know.

questions.prompt: A library has 312 books checked out. 98 are returned. How many are still checked out?
A garden has 56 red flowers and 47 yellow flowers. About how many flowers total?
questions.hint: 56 ≈ 60, 47 ≈ 50, estimate 110; or round to nearest hundred ~100.

questions.prompt: A bakery made 150 cupcakes. It sold 45 in the morning and 38 in the afternoon. How many are left?

learn.title: Ready to Show What You Know
teaching_points: Use any strategy that helps you.

example.prompt: You have learned four big ideas this unit.
example.equation: choose operation + estimate + one-step + two-step = problem solving

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Which operation solves: A team has 24 players. 9 leave. How many are left?

practice_block.title: Unit Evaluation
practice_block.instructions: Answer all questions carefully to show your understanding.

flashcards.title: Unit 8 Review
flashcards.instructions: Review key terms from Unit 8 before the evaluation.

bigIdea.title: Unit Evaluation: Addition and Subtraction Applications
bigIdea.subtitle: Show what you know
bigIdea.intro: This evaluation checks your understanding of the four big ideas from this unit: choosing an operation, estimating, one-step problems, and two-step problems with unknowns.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: What do you know about addition and subtraction problem solving?

ruleCards.description: Decide whether the problem is asking you to add, subtract, or both.
For two-step problems, solve one action before the next.
